## Linear Programming Model


```{=typst}
#import "@preview/equate:0.3.2": equate   // use the latest version from Typst Universe
#show: equate
#set math.equation(numbering: "(1)")
```

```{=typst}
$
  max quad & sum_(j=1)^n c_j x_j #label("ob") \
  "s.t." quad & sum_(j=1)^n a_(i j) x_j >= b_i, quad i = 1, dots.h, m #label("c1") \
  & x_j >= 0, quad j = 1, dots.h, n #label("c2")
$
```


We simulate data.

```{python}
#| label: fig-mat
#| fig-cap: "Simulated data for the constraint matrix."

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
n = 20
m = 10

A = rng.uniform(0, 10, (m, n))

print(A) 

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 6))
plt.imshow(A, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest", cmap="viridis")
plt.colorbar(label="Value")
plt.xlabel("Column")
plt.ylabel("Constraint Index")
#plt.xticks([0, 1], ["Intercept", "x"])
plt.title("Constraint matrix A")
plt.show()
```
